q: Of PA34's 1,213-gene accessory genome (1,206 in our rerun), what fraction is carried on demonstrably mobile elements (plasmids pMKPA34-1/-2 + the 24 RGPs including MKPA34-GI1 phage-associated island and MKPA34-GI2 phage MP38 + the three pKLC102/PAPI-1-like ICEs at RGP5/RGP29/RGP41) versus what is on stably vertically inherited but PA34-lineage-specific chromosomal loci, and does the mobile-borne fraction preferentially encode ocular-adaptation functions (biofilm, T3SS, iron scavenging, antimicrobial resistance) rather than the pulmonary CF-lineage adaptive-evolution signatures (loss of quorum sensing, mucoidy conversion via mucA mutations, hypermutator alleles) that dominate the adaptive-evolution literature for chronic-lung P. aeruginosa?
basis: Subedi et al. 2019 (PLoS ONE 14(4):e0215038) reports PA34 accessory = 1,213 genes with 543 unique and identifies 24 RGPs including two novel islands (MKPA34-GI1 68.6 kbp chromate+Hg; MKPA34-GI2 35.9 kbp phage MP38), three ICEs, plus a 125 kbp phage-derived AMR island RGP23; both plasmids are mobile-element-rich. REPORT.md verifies all named loci at their stated coordinates but does not partition the full 1,206-gene accessory set into 'mobile-borne' vs 'stably chromosomal PA34-specific' bins, and no comparison is made to the well-known CF-lung adaptive-evolution genomic signatures.
next_steps: Re-annotate CP032552 + MH547560 + MH547561 with a mobile-element pipeline (ICEfinder2 + MOB-suite + PHASTER + IslandViewer4), intersect the resulting mobile-element intervals with the 1,206 accessory-genome CDS coordinates from work/pangenome_pa34.py to compute the mobile-borne fraction, then run KEGG/eggNOG functional enrichment on (mobile-borne accessory) vs (chromosomal-non-mobile accessory) with ocular-adaptation and CF-lung-adaptation gene lists as two separate reference sets (Winstanley/Klockgether/Marvig CF-evolution reviews for the pulmonary panel; Fleiszig/Willcox/Green corneal-keratitis reviews for the ocular panel).

q: Where does PA34 sit in the global P. aeruginosa phylogenomic structure relative to the PAO1 clade, the PA14 clade, and the ocular VRFPA04 lineage (the paper's three chosen references), and does PA34 belong to a monophyletic keratitis-associated clonal complex (evidence for a globally expanding ocular lineage) or is it a phylogenetically independent keratitis isolate whose MDR + accessory-genome profile arose by convergent local acquisition in Hyderabad rather than by clonal descent?
basis: REPORT.md notes PA34 is 'MLST ST1284 - not tested here' (out of scope because PGAP annotations don't carry the traditional acsA/aroE/guaA/mutL/nuoD/ppsA/trpE gene tags), and the paper's own comparison is limited to PAO1/PA14/VRFPA04. The directional finding that VRFPA04 shares fewest orthologs with PA34 despite both being ocular isolates reproduces in our rerun (855/701/1,007 no-ortho vs PAO1/PA14/VRFPA04), which is suggestive of phylogenetic independence between the two ocular strains but is not proof.
next_steps: Run mlst (Seemann) against the PubMLST P. aeruginosa scheme to confirm ST1284 vs re-derive it, then place PA34 on a core-genome SNP tree built with Parsnp or a Roary + IQ-TREE core-alignment tree using a representative set of 200-500 P. aeruginosa complete genomes stratified by isolation source (ocular, CF-lung, wound, environmental) from NCBI + PubMLST + BV-BRC; overlay isolation-source metadata to test whether keratitis isolates cluster monophyletically or are polyphyletic, and quantify clonal-complex assignments (eBURST or PopPUNK) to test for a globally expanding ocular clonal complex.

q: What is the complete PA34 MDR resistome (integrating chromosomal + plasmid loci: AAC(3)-IId in RGP23, dfrA15/cmlA1/APH(3")-Ib/APH(6)-Id/blaNPS-1/acrB in class-I integron In1427 on pMKPA34-1 in a Tn3-like transposon, mepA + Tn7 on pMKPA34-2, plus BV-BRC-called AAC(3)-IIa/IIc, ampC/PDC-3, and multiple mex efflux operons), how does that resistome partition mechanistically across efflux + porin-loss + target-modification + enzymatic inactivation, and what fraction of the AMR determinants are horizontally acquired (integron/transposon/plasmid/phage-derived) versus PA34-lineage chromosomal mutation, and does the horizontally acquired fraction match the empirical MDR phenotype the paper attributes to PA34?
basis: REPORT.md verifies six plasmid AMR genes on pMKPA34-1 (+sul1 + qacEdelta1 bonuses + intI1 + Tn3 tnpR), mepA + full Tn7 module on pMKPA34-2, and AAC(3)-IId + tunicamycin + copper resistance + phage gp37 in the 125 kbp RGP23 chromosomal island. The BV-BRC PATRIC pipeline independently returns 251 antibiotic-resistance annotations. But the paper does not itself perform a horizontal-vs-mutational partition of the resistome, does not report which mex efflux operons carry expression-activating mutations (nalC/nalD/mexZ/mexR/nfxB regulator lesions), and does not link individual determinants to the observed MIC panel.
next_steps: Run CARD-RGI (strict + loose + variant-model) plus AMRFinderPlus + ResFinder against CP032552 + MH547560 + MH547561 to build a triangulated resistome; call SNPs/indels in mex-operon regulators (nalC, nalD, mexZ, mexR, nfxB) and in the ampC promoter/attenuator against PAO1 as reference to distinguish acquired from mutational determinants; intersect determinant positions with the mobile-element intervals from the mobilome pipeline (question 1) to compute the horizontally acquired fraction; compare the predicted resistance-phenotype panel to the paper's cited MIC data where available, and note where mutational contributions (e.g. oprD porin loss for carbapenems) may be under-appreciated.

q: When PA34's virulence-factor repertoire (functional exoU cytotoxin + SpcU chaperone in RGP7, pyoverdine biosynthesis/export replacement island at RGP73, flagellin replacement at RGP9, plus the standard core-genome T3SS/quorum-sensing/biofilm apparatus) is compared as a gene-signature to matched panels of ocular-keratitis isolates, environmental water/soil isolates, and pulmonary CF isolates, which loci are ocular-adaptation-enriched (expected: exoU T3SS effector strongly enriched in keratitis; iron-scavenging pyoverdine variants tuned to lacrimal/corneal iron limitation; biofilm-matrix Psl/Pel variants tuned to contact-lens surfaces) versus generic P. aeruginosa virulence, and does PA34 carry any keratitis-specific virulence signatures not previously reported in the ocular-isolate literature?
basis: REPORT.md verifies exoU at chromosome position 4,720,713 with SpcU chaperone at 4,720,303 (inside RGP7 4,719,909-4,727,427), pyoverdine NRPS at 2,988,776 and export at 3,061,910-3,065,331 (flanking RGP73), and flagellin at 4,600,486 (adjacent to RGP9). Fig 5 shows PA34 is high-cytotoxic to HCECs but this is out of scope for a public-data replication (not attempted here). The paper does not compare PA34's virulence loci to matched ocular vs environmental vs CF panels, and does not report contact-lens-specific biofilm-matrix variants.
next_steps: Build three matched panels (~30 genomes each) of ocular-keratitis, environmental, and CF-chronic isolates from NCBI/BV-BRC with clean source metadata; extract the T3SS effector suite (exoU/S/T/Y), pyoverdine biosynthesis + siderophore-receptor cluster, quorum-sensing regulators (lasR/rhlR/pqsR intact-vs-mutated), and biofilm-matrix operons (pel, psl, cdrA); test per-locus enrichment (Fisher exact + Benjamini-Hochberg) of PA34-carried alleles across the three source classes; publish the ocular-signature panel; separately, sequence-search PA34 for any accessory locus (from the 1,206 accessory set) with a keratitis-only distribution across the panel to nominate keratitis-specific virulence candidates.

q: Given PA34's phage MP38 in the novel MKPA34-GI2 island (35.9 kbp) plus the phage gp37 insertion in the 125 kbp RGP23 AMR island plus the two plasmid-borne phage integrase/resolvase modules on pMKPA34-2, and given the absence of a functional CRISPR-Cas defense system consistent with the paper's inflated-accessory-genome interpretation, which characterized therapeutic P. aeruginosa phages (the classical Pf/JG/PAK/LKD/PAJU2/LKA phages, the recent Cystophage/Locusphage clinical panels, and the PhagoBurn/Adaptive Phage Therapeutics compassionate-use panels) predict productive-infection on PA34, and which PA34 accessory-genome loci constitute the most likely resistance-evolution escape routes (receptor-loss mutations in LPS O-antigen/Type-IV pilus/OMPs, restriction-modification gain, integrated-prophage superinfection immunity from MP38, abortive-infection systems in the mobilome)?
basis: REPORT.md verifies phage MP38 in MKPA34-GI2, phage gp37 at chromosome position 3,314,352 inside RGP23, and phage-integrase + resolvase modules on pMKPA34-2. The paper explicitly notes the CRISPR-Cas absence as consistent with PA34's inflated accessory genome. PA34's MDR + keratitis clinical origin makes it a natural test case for adjunctive phage therapy in MDR bacterial keratitis, an active clinical-translation area, but the paper does not perform any phage-susceptibility prediction and does not inventory phage-resistance evolution loci.
next_steps: Run PhageBoost + PHASTER + geNomad on CP032552 + both plasmids to complete the prophage inventory (MP38 + any missed prophages); host-range-predict a curated therapeutic-phage panel against PA34 using Kaptive (LPS/O-antigen typing), spacer-independent host-range models (PHIST, HostPhinder, or the Edwards-lab RaFAH tool), and receptor-gene BLAST (Type-IV pilus PilA allelic type, LPS wzy/wbp cluster, OprM/OprF variants); score PA34 accessory loci for known phage-resistance functions (BREX, DISARM, RM systems, retrons, Wadjet, Thoerter, abortive-infection modules) using the DefenseFinder + PADLOC pipelines; rank candidate therapeutic phages by predicted productive-infection likelihood and by the number of independent PA34-side escape routes, publish the top-3 phage cocktail nomination for MDR-keratitis pre-clinical evaluation.
